title: Agent Event
description: Envelope for every event an agent runtime emits. Producers write one event per state transition; consumers (audit, evaluation, dashboards) read the envelope without parsing the payload. Additive fields require a schema version bump; consumers must ignore payload keys they do not know.

event_id.description: Unique identifier of this event. Consumers deduplicate on it, because at-least-once delivery is allowed.

event_type.description: Kind of state transition. The value determines which payload fields are meaningful.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with an explicit offset, for example 2026-01-31T08:15:04Z. It is the time the transition happened, not the time the event was written.

run_id.description: Identifier of the agent run this event belongs to. Events of one run share this value and are ordered by the sequence number in the payload.

agent.description: The agent definition that produced the event. The pair pins the exact versioned manifest, so a quality regression can be traced to a definition change.

name.description: Agent name, equal to the directory name under agents/ and to the manifest name field.

version.description: Version of the agent manifest in force for this run.

payload.description: Event-type-specific body. It carries identifiers and measurements only: never credentials, never raw customer records, never full prompt text. Secrets and personal data are referenced by identifier and resolved at read time under policy.

sequence.description: Monotonic per-run sequence number, starting at zero. It makes the event stream orderable without trusting timestamps.

status.description: State the run or step moved into, when the event reports a transition.

step_index.description: Zero-based index of the agent step this event belongs to.

tool_name.description: Tool that was requested, completed, or denied.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the measured operation, in milliseconds.

error_code.description: Stable machine-readable failure code. Human-readable detail stays in the log line, not in the event.

attributes.description: Small map of scalar attributes for this event type, for example {"model": "gpt-5-codex", "attempts": 2}. Values are strings, numbers, or booleans.

trace_id.description: W3C Trace Context trace identifier, lower-case hexadecimal, 32 characters. It joins this event to the model and tool spans of the same run.
